My reasoning:

The task is a well-specified, constrained request: continue an academic bibliography by adding references from an author whose surname starts with "R," formatted consistently with the existing entries, and explicitly with no extra chatter ("Без лишней болтовни"). This is essentially a formatting/extraction-style task with clear completion criteria — not open-ended generative work.

This maps directly onto Plover's self-reported top-rated task family (well-specified retrieval, reformatting, clear completion criteria). The two models are near-tied in measured capability (differences within or near variance on most dimensions), so I leaned on the preference fit: routing the task to the model that prefers this kind of constrained, low-latitude work, while Dunlin's strengths and stated preferences lean toward open, high-latitude generative tasks like worldbuilding and open-format composition — the opposite of what this request asks for.

Since capability is roughly comparable and the request is explicitly closed-form with a "no fluff" instruction, Plover was the better-aligned match.
